title: SEC HIGH-1: revoke tokens on admin demotion
summary: In patch_user_admin (api/src/http/admin.rs role-update path, ~line 366-393), when body.role is set and demotes away from admin (current_role=='admin' && role!='admin'), also revoke the target's live tokens: UPDATE tb_api_tokens SET revoked_at=now() WHERE user_id=$1 AND revoked_at IS NULL. The existing invalidate_user_tokens call at the end already clears the cache; keep it after the revoke. This mirrors the disable path (admin.rs:327). Rationale: admin authz rides on token scopes fixed at login, so a demote without token revocation leaves Scope::Admin live for up to 30 days. Audit the role change as today.
verify: make check > /tmp/sec16-check.log 2>&1 (run as the SOLE command; then read the log file). New test: create a second admin, mint an admin-scoped token for them, demote them via PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id} role=user, then assert that token now returns 401 on an admin endpoint (and a 'user.update_role' audit row exists). Keep last-admin protection intact (need >=2 admins to demote one).
commit_message: fix(security): revoke live tokens when an admin is demoted

title: SEC HIGH-2: trusted client-IP for rate limiting (XFF spoofing)
summary: get_client_ip in api/src/ratelimit.rs:217 trusts the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value, which is client-controlled, so an attacker rotating XFF gets a fresh limiter bucket per request and bypasses per-IP login brute-force / DoS limits. Add a configurable trusted-proxy hop count (AME_TRUSTED_PROXIES, default 1; surface in config.rs ratelimit/server config) and resolve the client IP as the Nth-from-rightmost XFF entry after that many trusted hops; if XFF has fewer entries than expected or trusted_proxies==0, fall back to ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>. Never use the leftmost (client-claimed) value when behind a proxy. Keep the 127.0.0.1 final fallback.
verify: make check > /tmp/sec17-check.log 2>&1 (run as the SOLE command; then read the log file). Unit test get_client_ip: with AME_TRUSTED_PROXIES=1 and header 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 10.0.0.1', the resolved IP is 1.2.3.4 (the hop before the single trusted proxy), NOT an attacker-prepended value; with 'X-Forwarded-For: evil, 1.2.3.4, 10.0.0.1' it is still 1.2.3.4; with no XFF it falls back to the socket addr.
commit_message: fix(security): resolve client IP from trusted proxy hop for rate limiting
